title: The Orbit of the Deep
premise: Cyrus Okonkwo has spent two decades smuggling memories past orbital customs, staying small enough that no faction bothers to kill her. When the research vessel Halcyon returns from a deep-space jump with its crew aged backward into children who retain fragmented adult memories, Cyrus is the only courier both sides of the war trust — or fear — enough to carry what the ship carries: proof that the jump drive's inventor deliberately seeded the return with a message that could end the war. As customs fleets, memory cartels, and the children themselves hunt her, Cyrus must choose between selling the message to the highest bidder and delivering it intact, knowing its release will expose her own buried role in the drive's creation. In the final chapter, she broadcasts the message from inside the closing jump window, sacrificing her anonymity and her ship, and the ceasefire holds — but only because she finally admits what she did twenty years ago.
about_author: Orsen Zhou is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years on container ships before turning to fiction, and his work often explores people who live in the gaps between jurisdictions. He writes from a houseboat in an undisclosed harbor.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. A routine smuggling run through Meridian Station customs introduces Cyrus's world: forged memory-chips hidden in coolant tanks, bribed inspectors, and her partner Doss keeping the ledger. The emotional beat is weary competence — Cyrus is good at being invisible, and the chapter quietly shows how much that invisibility has cost her.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back Young
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Dockworkers flag the Halcyon drifting into orbit, transponder dark; boarding it, Cyrus finds a crew of children wearing adult rank insignia and speaking in fragments of classified jargon. One girl, Ada, recognizes Cyrus by name. The beat is dread: something impossible has arrived, and it knows her.

chapters.title: Twenty Years Gone
chapters.summary: POV Ada (the child-crew). Ada's fractured memories surface in dreams — a launch, a jump, screaming instruments, and a woman's voice ordering the crew sealed in cryo 'for their own protection.' She wakes convinced the voice belonged to someone on Meridian. The beat is disorientation and grief for lives lived twice.

chapters.title: Customs Wants a Word
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Warlord-administrator Vey Kessler detains Cyrus, offering amnesty for one job: recover whatever the Halcyon brought back before the rival Concordat does. Cyrus refuses and walks out — then finds her smuggling routes frozen within hours. The beat is the trap closing: neutrality was always rented, never owned.

chapters.title: What the Children Carry
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Under quarantine, the child-crew's shared memories begin syncing through proximity, reconstructing the mission piece by piece. Ada realizes the ship's data core was wiped but that Dr. Sefa Ilić hid the true record inside the crew's own implanted memories. The beat is dawning purpose: they are not survivors, they are the cargo.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Hiding the children in a decommissioned fuel depot, Cyrus weighs selling them to Kessler against a Concordat bounty. Doss argues for the money; Cyrus discovers one recovered fragment shows her own younger face at the drive's christening. The beat is self-betrayal surfacing — the past she smuggled away is coming due.

chapters.title: Ilić's Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Following memory-cues, Ada locates Dr. Ilić's hidden lab aboard the derelict Halcyon and plays his final recording: the jump works, but each transit erases years, and he aged the crew backward deliberately so the message would be carried by witnesses no court would execute. The beat is awe curdling into anger at being used.

chapters.title: A Price Quoted in Blood
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Kessler's enforcers raid the depot; Cyrus buys the children's escape by burning her ship and her cover identity, going from invisible to hunted in one night. Doss takes a bullet covering the retreat. The beat is loss and irrevocability — survival now requires becoming exactly what she avoided being: visible.

chapters.title: The Concordat's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Concordat spymaster Rell Anwar offers Cyrus sanctuary, a new ship, and protection — in exchange for the message, which the Concordat intends to weaponize as leverage, not peace. Cyrus stalls, recognizing the same corruption she fled in Kessler wearing a cleaner uniform. The beat is temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Children of the Jump
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The synced memories complete: Ilić's message is a full confession that the war's opening strike was staged using stolen jump telemetry — evidence that indicts both governments' founders. Ada must decide whether children can be trusted to testify to a truth adults will kill to bury. The beat is resolve hardening into responsibility.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Buried
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cornered by her own recovered fragment, Cyrus confesses to Ada: twenty years ago she was Ilić's lab assistant who helped fake the telemetry that started the war, then erased her own memory of it and sold fragments of herself ever since. The beat is shame met without absolution — Ada refuses to forgive, only to use her.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Window
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Both fleets converge on Meridian as the next jump window opens in nine days; whoever controls the window controls whether the message can be broadcast system-wide through the relay lattice. The children become pawns in a standoff neither admiral fully understands. The beat is claustrophobic escalation.

chapters.title: The Cartel Cuts In
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The memory cartel Cyrus once supplied kidnaps three of the child-crew, planning to strip and sell their implanted evidence piecemeal. Cyrus negotiates with her old handler, Maro, trading the location of her last unlogged cache for the children — and learns Maro already sold the cartel's allegiance to Kessler. The beat is betrayal compounding betrayal.

chapters.title: Raid on the Gullet
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Cyrus and Ada lead a desperate extraction through the station's pressurized underlevels, the 'Gullet,' where Ada's recovered piloting memories let them fly a maintenance skiff through spaces no current charts remember. They escape with two children; one is lost. The beat is grief sharpening commitment.

chapters.title: Anwar's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Anwar reveals the Concordat knew about the staged strike all along and has been managing the war's tempo for profit; he offers Cyrus a place in the arrangement rather than punishment. Cyrus understands the message won't end the war by exposure alone — power absorbs truth unless it's delivered all at once, publicly, everywhere. The beat is strategic clarity born of disgust.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Preparations: the remaining children rehearse testimony while Cyrus refits a captured tug with broadcast capability and plots a path through the relay lattice. Kessler and Anwar, briefly allied, seal the station. The beat is quiet before the storm — tenderness among the children contrasting the machinery closing around them.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Sky
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus confronts Maro atop the relay spine and finds him dying, having double-crossed Kessler too; he gives her the master access key and a warning: the lattice will burn out anyone who broadcasts from inside it. She accepts the cost silently. The beat is a thief's redemption priced in advance.

chapters.title: Window Opening
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The jump window begins; both fleets maneuver for position as Cyrus's tug slips the cordon using a dead-signal ghost profile Ada reconstructed from crew memory. Kessler's flagship detects them at the worst moment. The beat is kinetic desperation — everything staked on a trajectory that shouldn't work.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Inside the lattice, Cyrus plugs in Ilić's confession and her own testimony alongside it, naming herself as the forger. The broadcast floods every screen in contested space as the lattice begins cooking the tug's systems. The beat is catharsis through confession — she ends the war's lie by ending her own.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at the Edge of the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Ada. With both fleets' founding lies exposed simultaneously, admirals stand down rather than fight for a cause proven fraudulent; Kessler tries to seize the children and is abandoned by her own officers. The jump window closes on an armistice signed in the Halcyon's old mess hall. The beat is exhausted, untriumphant relief.

chapters.title: Aging Forward
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Weeks later, the child-crew faces a choice: experimental treatment to restore their lost years, or adoption and ordinary childhoods. Ada chooses her own timeline, adopting the others' right to choose differently. Cyrus, stripped of rank and wealth, asks nothing. The beat is healing without erasure — memory kept, price paid.

chapters.title: The Orbit of the Deep
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus takes a legitimate hauling contract on a slow freighter, passing the Halcyon's restored hulk in permanent memorial orbit. Ada sends her a single memory chip: not evidence, just a recorded thank-you. Cyrus finally plays her own pre-erasure memories, weeps, and lets them stay. The beat is peace earned by carrying the whole weight of the past.
